issues.description: The problem statement / UML explicitly specifies the Animal.name attribute as type String, but the reference solution defines the field as a StringBuilder (private StringBuilder name). This is a structural attribute type mismatch that deviates from the specification and could confuse students about the expected attribute type and how to implement getter/setter semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the String type for the Animal.name attribute in the solution (and any templates) to match the UML and problem description. Change the field in Animal.java to 'private String name;' and adjust constructor/getter/setter accordingly (or update the problem statement/UML to explicitly allow StringBuilder if that was intended).

issues.description: The UML and problem description indicate a private helper singFarmSongVerse should accept an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)), and the solution implements this signature. However, the template's Farm.java currently defines singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter commented out (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), meaning the template's method signature does not match the specified/expected signature. This mismatch may confuse students about the intended method signature and how to call it from singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment or add the Animal parameter in the template's singFarmSongVerse signature so it matches the UML and solution (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This makes the template consistent with the specification and reduces confusion when students implement singFarmSong() and call the helper.
